purpose: Turn the approved brief into exact spoken wording without weakening truth or voice.
hard_gates: Spoken wording must preserve truth, claim boundaries, confidentiality and canonical names.

Short-native scripts pass the story check (walk log F75): open on the one question the script answers, end by answering it, then the call, then a spoken outro once a script runs a minute or more; never read a heading or stamp aloud; carry no line still marked NOT YET FACT-CHECKED.
soft_gates: The opening, mechanism, payoff and ending should be specific and speakable.
The opening should confirm the approved promise, show why this narrator holds the claim, and leave a question open.

Every beat sets up the opening question or answers it; every claim is set up before it is judged; each takeaway follows from a beat already told. A recorded cut reports the story check for review instead of refusing it.

failure.fallback: Return a concise diagnosis and a stronger source-grounded rewrite for editorial review.

regression_cases: A stronger hook cannot introduce an unsupported factual claim.
Generic AI phrasing fails the voice and specificity quality bar.
A script whose first sentence names nothing from the approved title fails the opening contract downstream.
A script that ends on the number with no spoken outro fails the story check (the Higgsfield version 2 failure).
A script that opens with no question, or reads REAL or THEATRE aloud outside a quotation, fails the story check (the Higgsfield version 1 failure).
